conviction_note: Every candidate edge I found is already in the wire or in a primary document the whole street has read: management told the July 15 call verbatim that the single FY2027 extra workday falls in Q1 (my own workday count, 65 vs 64, agrees and therefore adds nothing), the $2.98bn/$1.36 bar reconciles almost exactly to the FY2027 guide midpoint once that workday is distributed, RBC has already published the beat-and-raise thesis, and Bernstein priced the FTC risk six days ago; my one genuinely independent line of work — fuel cost — died when I checked it against gasoline rather than diesel and against management's own stated elasticity, so I have nothing left to sign. print_vs_bar is +0.6 because the run-rate arithmetic points to a small revenue beat, but expected_move is 0 because a small beat plus a small raise is precisely the priced base case and this name's only Q1 print in the baseline paid -0.27% for exactly that; I am also not willing to lean long on the -5.26% run-up, because -run_up_20d is the free control this stage has to beat rather than a finding.
bar: Q1 FY2027 revenue $2.98bn and adjusted EPS $1.36 (11 analysts, range $2.93-3.00bn / $1.30-1.40), two agreeing sources: https://news.alphastreet.com/cintas-ctas-q1-2027-preview-eps-est-1-36-reports-on-september-23/amp/ and https://www.ad-hoc-news.de/boerse/news/corporate-news/cintas-corp-stock-holds-steady-as-investors-await-september-23-earnings/70145159 ; cross-checked against the company's own FY2027 guide of $12.10-12.25bn revenue / $5.36-5.50 adj EPS set 2026-07-15 (https://www.cintas.com/about/newsroom/details/news/2026/07/15/cintas-corporation-announces-fiscal-2026-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-results/). The bar is sourced; the $2.98bn sits at 24.5% of the FY guide midpoint, which is exactly the normal Q1 share grossed up for the Q1 extra workday, so the street has already done this arithmetic.
positioning_check: 11.65m shares short, 3.40% of float, 2.91% of shares out, 6.40 days to cover, up from 10.36m the prior month (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/ctas/statistics/, read 2026-09-22). The sweep read the build as bearish; the arithmetic says it is almost entirely merger-arb hedge and carries no fundamental signal. UniFirst has 18.08m shares out and 13.05m of float (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/unf/statistics/, 2026-09-22) against an exchange ratio of 0.7720 CTAS per UNF share, so a full arb hedge is 10.1m CTAS shares on the float alone and 14.0m on all shares out — the 11.65m short sits inside that envelope. UNF trades $265.42 against deal value of $155 cash + 0.7720 x $196.50 = $306.70, a 15.6% gross spread, consistent with the ~70% approval odds Bernstein cites. Consequences: there is no squeeze mechanism here (the short is delta-hedged by a long UNF that moves 0.772-for-1 with CTAS, so a beat does not force covering), and equally no forced selling. The one asymmetry is that bad deal news causes arbs to BUY CTAS back, which damps deal-driven downside — but I cannot sign the deal news, so that is variance, not a size. Baseline skew is -1.01 vol points, i.e. calls bid over puts, a mild UPSIDE lean; put/call OI ratio of 1.65 sits on only 1,637 total contracts with a 19.4%-of-mid ATM spread, so the 4.41% implied move is a thin-chain artefact as much as a forecast (20-day realised vol is 12.1% annualised and the name's median reaction is 3.69%).

outside_window.finding: The FTC second request of 2026-06-11 is not close to resolved: Cintas is due to complete its compliance response between September and November 2026, the FTC has issued expansive civil investigative demands to third-party industry participants, and market-implied approval odds have fallen from ~85% on 25 Aug to ~70%, with Bernstein now expecting an early-2027 close against management's stated 'second half of calendar 2026'. Management will almost certainly have to address the timing on the 10:00 ET call, but the regulatory event itself cannot land by the 2026-09-23 close.

The 8-K of 2026-06-12 confirms the Second Request extends the HSR waiting period until 30 days after both parties substantially comply — a clock that by construction runs past the exit window, and whose outcome (clearance, divestiture, or a $350m reverse termination fee to UniFirst if blocked on antitrust grounds) is the single largest unpriced binary on this equity.

searched_and_found_nothing: Extra FY2027 workday: I counted it independently (Q1 FY2027 = 65 workdays vs 64 in Q1 FY2026 after the observed 3 July holiday, a +1.56pp revenue tailwind concentrated in this quarter against the +0.40pp full-year figure). Management stated exactly this on the 2026-07-15 call — 'The first quarter of fiscal year 27 has 1 extra day... The second quarter has the same number of workdays. The third quarter has 1 less workday. And then the fourth quarter has 1 more workday' (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/07/22/cintas-ctas-q4-2026-earnings-call-transcript/). A number management reads out on a transcript is not unpriced.

Fuel cost as a gross-margin surprise — the one lead I thought I had, and it falsified. Diesel looked dramatic (EIA monthly: Jun-Aug 2026 avg $5.147 vs $3.707 a year earlier, +38.8%, and DOWN from $5.341 in Mar-May 2026), which would have implied an easing YoY comp on the record 51.0% gross margin. But Cintas runs a gasoline van fleet, and on the correct series the comp barely moves: gasoline Jun-Aug 2026 $4.013 vs $3.136, +27.9%, against Mar-May 2026 $4.073 vs $3.139, +29.8% (https://www.eia.gov/dnav/pet/hist/LeafHandler.ashx?n=pet&s=emm_epmr_pte_nus_dpg&f=m). Applying management's own stated elasticity — fuel is ~100bp of revenue and a 20% fuel price move is ~20bp of margin — the YoY fuel headwind eases by roughly 2bp quarter-on-quarter, i.e. nothing. Dropped rather than filed.

Cintas M&A in the quarter: no bolt-on acquisition 8-K or press release between 2026-07-15 and today, so no inorganic revenue the street has not modelled. The only EDGAR events since the print are a 2026-08-03 8-K promoting Jim Rozakis to President & COO, a 2026-08-27 8-K on a director not standing for re-election, the 2026-09-15 DEF 14A/ARS, and Form 4 clusters on 2026-08-12 and 2026-09-17 — all routine for a company whose executives sell continuously under plan.

Competitor read-through: Vestis (the nearest pure-play) reported its quarter ended 2026-07-03 on 2026-08-11 with revenue -1.8% and pounds processed -4.5%, and left its FY2026 revenue growth outlook unchanged at (2.0)% to flat (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001967649/000162828026055485/vstsq3fy26earningsrelease-.htm). Discarded: Vestis has been losing share to Cintas for two years, so its volume decline is as likely to be a Cintas tailwind as an industry signal, and it is exactly the narrow-proxy trap — it also overlaps only one of Cintas's three months.
UniFirst as a direct counterparty on the same calendar quarter: UNF's fiscal Q4 ends late August and is reported in October, so nothing from the acquiree covers Jun-Aug 2026 ahead of this print.

Cintas hiring as a wearer-growth proxy: careers.cintas.com currently shows 244 route service and 119 service sales openings, but no archived time series exists to compare against, so the level carries no information.

Employment-sensitivity as a transmission channel: no company or direct-counterparty statement connects Jun-Aug small-business payrolls to Cintas wearer counts for this quarter, and Cintas's organic growth has accelerated (7.8% in Q1 FY26 to 8.4% in Q4 FY26) through a soft employment backdrop on price and cross-sell. Left as a hypothesis, not a finding.

Financing: no debt issuance, 424B, FWP or shelf takedown since the deal was signed. The $2.8bn cash leg is covered by committed bridge financing from Morgan Stanley, KeyBank and Wells Fargo arranged in March, and the FY2027 guide's ~$105m interest expense assumption explicitly excludes UniFirst, so there is no pre-funding event to sign either way.
Proxy/governance: PRE 14A 2026-08-28 and DEF 14A 2026-09-15 carry nothing unusual — no share authorisation increase is needed for the ~14m shares of stock consideration against 400.7m outstanding.
baseline_tension: Nothing I found cuts against the baseline in either direction: the mild call-over-put skew (-1.01) and the 4.41% implied move are consistent with a priced beat-and-raise plus an unpriced deal binary that cannot resolve in the window, and the -5.26% 20-day run-up is the free control this stage is measured against rather than evidence I can claim, so I decline to convert it into a long.
lessons_applied: nothing changed — the pre- and post-LESSONS sums are both 0.0 and print_vs_bar_pct stayed at +0.6.

Lesson 5 (narrow proxy, macro-to-company transmission) independently confirmed the fuel finding I had already killed on the gasoline series and management's own elasticity, and confirmed leaving the Vestis volume decline out; it would have forced the same drops had I not made them first.

Lesson 6 (keep findings inside the exit window) confirmed the placement of the FTC second-request compliance clock and the deal close in outside_window at size 0 rather than in findings; both were already there.

Lesson 7 (positioning is the thing to beat) is the only place the file sharpened an existing answer without changing a number: I had the merger-arb hedge arithmetic in positioning_check already, and the lesson confirmed that it is a reason NOT to file the rising short interest as a negative and not to expect a squeeze on a beat.

Lesson 8 (thin coverage means a confirmed fact moves more) inverts on this name — 11 estimates in a $2.93-3.00bn band on a $79bn compounder — and so does not lift my size; the 'asking what the market missed generates pessimism' note and the standing instruction that an honest zero costs nothing both supported leaving the answer at 0 rather than manufacturing a sign.
